classification.difficultyReason: Split exactly one accident into two disjoint cases, pair each accident probability with the other person's no-accident probability, then add the products.

content.prompt: An insurance company has calculated that, in a given year, the probability of a 20-year-old woman having a car accident is $0.3$ and the probability of a 20-year-old man having a car accident is $0.6$. A 20-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman are chosen at random. Assume that whether each person has an accident that year is independent of whether the other person does. What is the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: they will both have an accident that year?

answer.worked:
The two accident events are independent.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{both})&=0.3\times 0.6\\P(\text{both})&=\frac{9}{50}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: only one of them will have an accident that year?

answer.worked:
Only the woman has an accident, or only the man has an accident. These cases are mutually exclusive.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one})&=0.3(1-0.6)+(1-0.3)0.6\\P(\text{exactly one})&=0.3\times 0.4+0.7\times 0.6\\P(\text{exactly one})&=0.12+0.42\\P(\text{exactly one})&=\frac{27}{50}\end{align*}$$
